title: Grade 6 French — Mon, May 18
description: Les chiffres et les nombres (Numbers) — Day 1 of 5: 1–20
subject: french

questions.question: What is the French word for the number 1?
questions.explanation: 'Un' (masculine) / 'Une' (feminine) = 1. Example: 'J'ai un frère' = I have one brother.

questions.question: How do you write 5 in French?
questions.explanation: 'Cinq' = 5. Pronunciation tip: the 'q' at the end is pronounced, unlike in 'cinq cents' (500) where it is silent.

questions.question: What number does 'dix' represent?
questions.explanation: 'Dix' = 10. This root appears in many larger numbers: dix-sept (17), dix-huit (18), dix-neuf (19).

questions.question: How do you say 11 in French?
questions.explanation: 'Onze' = 11. Note: 11-16 have unique names (onze, douze, treize, quatorze, quinze, seize) — they don't follow the pattern of adding 'dix-'.

questions.question: What is 'quatorze' in numbers?
questions.explanation: 'Quatorze' = 14. Pattern for 11-16: onze(11), douze(12), treize(13), quatorze(14), quinze(15), seize(16).

questions.question: Which of these is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: 'Dix' = 10, NOT 11. 'Onze' = 11. Be careful not to confuse these.

questions.question: How do you say 17 in French?
questions.explanation: 'Dix-sept' = 17 (literally 'ten-seven'). From 17-19, French adds to 'dix': dix-sept(17), dix-huit(18), dix-neuf(19).

questions.question: What does 'vingt' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Vingt' = 20. This is an important base number — vingt et un (21), vingt-deux (22), etc.

questions.question: 'J'ai seize ans.' What does this sentence mean?
questions.explanation: 'J'ai seize ans' = 'I am sixteen years old'. 'Seize' = 16, 'ans' = years. French uses 'avoir' (to have) for age.

questions.question: Count the sequence: un, deux, trois, ___. What comes next?
questions.explanation: The sequence 1, 2, 3 is followed by 4 = 'quatre'. Remember: un(1), deux(2), trois(3), quatre(4), cinq(5).

questions.question: What is the French word for zero?
questions.explanation: 'Zéro' = 0. It is borrowed from Arabic 'sifr' (also the origin of English 'zero'). Used in phone numbers, scores, etc.

questions.question: 'Il a douze crayons.' How many pencils does he have?
questions.explanation: 'Douze' = 12. 'Il a douze crayons' = 'He has twelve pencils'. 'Crayon' = pencil.

questions.question: How do you say 'eighteen' in French?
What is 'quinze' in numbers?
questions.explanation: 'Quinze' = 15. The pattern for teens: onze(11), douze(12), treize(13), quatorze(14), quinze(15), seize(16).
